messages:
Priya: urgent: observed spike of 429s on embed ingestion after last rollout. Root cause looks like regressed batching logic. Need hotfix and fast approvals. Suggest canary 5% for 5m then 25% then full. If 5xx or 429 rate > 0.6% rollback. ETA to patch build ~8m. Requesting expedited approvals now. @ops-oncall pls standby.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: image=gcr.io/redwood/serve:hotfix-embed-batch-2026-03-23-v1 target=prod/embed-ingest strategy=canary(5%,5m)->25%->100%. To approve: `/deploy approve 1825694000 --fastpath` or start: `/deploy start 1825694000 --canary 5m`. Runbook: /runbooks/embed-batch-hotfix (link).

Jonah: how bad is customer impact? Any errors > customers?

Priya: hit several downstream retries; B2B customers saw timeouts and increased client-side backoffs. Not P0 but definitely blocking some scheduled jobs.

Kelsey: +1 from SRE side if ops-oncall is good. Suggest cordon canary pool and set quick alert threshold for 429 to 0.5%.

ops-oncall: watching infra; prefer canary but if customer SLA impacted we can fastpath to 25% after 3m. I'm ready to flip rollback if things go south.

Luca: small ask: include release note blurb: "Fix batching regression causing 429 throttles for high-concurrency embeds." Also tag release manager.

Priya: building image now, pushing. Will request deploy in ~6m.

deploy-bot: image pushed: gcr.io/redwood/serve:hotfix-embed-batch-2026-03-23-v1.

Priya: executing `/deploy start 1825694000 --canary 5m --image hotfix-embed-batch-2026-03-23-v1` now. Pinning image to deployment id 1825694000.

deploy-bot: canary_started: 5% traffic -> 2 pods in us-west1. Hooks: latency, 429_rate, error_5xx.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics @ +2m: latency down 6%, 429_rate 0.3%. Good so far.

Jonah: telemetry looks healthier from traces.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics @ +4m: latency stable, 429_rate 0.45%, no 5xx. Ops-oncall, approve advance to 25%?

ops-oncall: go to 25% now.

deploy-bot: ramping to 25% -> 10 pods.

deploy-bot: Ramp metrics @ +90s: 429_rate 0.7% (threshold 0.6%). Alert: embed-ingest 429_rate above threshold.

Kelsey: :warning: threshold breached. ops-oncall do we want to drain canary or full rollback?

ops-oncall: drain traffic first (soft rollback) to be safe, then full rollback if metrics don't recover within 2m.

deploy-bot: draining canary: scaling canary pods down and shifting traffic away.

Priya: running quick smoke against canary endpoints to confirm.

deploy-bot: Drain complete. Canary pods terminated. Current 429_rate across prod back to baseline 0.2%.

Luca: thanks. Keep the failed image pinned to the incident for later analysis.

Priya: will open PR for revised batching with extra guardrails and add test covering high-concurrency path. Re-trigger will require more telemetry.

Jonah: +1 on tests. Good catch.

ops-oncall: closing fast response. No full rollback needed, traffic stabilized. Filing incident note and tagging postmortem. :white_check_mark:
